- **What broke:** On Thursday, November 12, ingest v2.14.0 raised the default batch size from 1 MB to 10 MB. Ingest workers with a 512 MiB memory limit ran out of memory and repeatedly crashed. The change had gone to every worker at once, and there was no consumer-lag alert; the first signal was an out-of-memory alert 27 minutes after deployment. [1]
- **Customer impact:** All workspaces saw stale dashboards from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC. The team rolled back at 10:05, and the backlog finished draining at 12:27. Events continued arriving in Kafka; reconciliation the next day matched workspace event counts to Kafka offsets and found **no lost events**. [1][5]
- **What’s changing:** The 1 MB default and a guard rejecting batches over 25% of container memory were merged on November 13. The follow-ups are canary-first configuration changes, raising worker memory to 1 GiB, and batch-size load testing. A consumer-lag alert is in place and routed to on-call, but the five-minute threshold is still being tuned because nightly backfills trigger it. [13][1][11]
